Formulation  
- Patient presents with recent onset (2 days) of lower abdominal pain described as burning, progressively worsening. Accompanying symptoms include pink-colored urine (uncertain hematuria), increased urinary frequency (likely due to increased fluid intake), mild nausea, and feeling hot/sweaty without measured fever. No significant past medical or family history. Social context stable with shared housing and employment as accountant. No mental health issues disclosed or assessed. Possible urinary tract infection or pregnancy-related cause considered. Empiric antibiotic treatment commenced with Trimethoprim. Advised pregnancy test and to monitor symptoms for escalation. No mental health symptoms observed or reported.
